notes:
ACCESS: plain requests return HTTP 403; curl_cffi with impersonate=chrome131 (probe.fetch, profiles pinned to chrome131/chrome124/chrome120) returned 200 on every URL - the same route the prior Furniture and Home-Decor passes on this SR used. No proxy, no WAF workaround. robots.txt names NO Anthropic/Claude/ClaudeBot agent; it disallows /*collection.do*, /*product.do*, /?method*, /*print.do*, /*error, /*reviews/submit.do*, /ajax/modal/, /modal/, /configurator/modal/, /blog/author|category|tag/, /resources/, /sitesearch/, /styleguide/*, /*features/* and /cdn-cgi/ - none of which I touched; every URL below is a plain /catalog/... path. robots.txt declares 'Crawl-delay: 10' for User-Agent: *, so I raised probe.py's default 2s per-host gap to an explicit 8s sleep plus the built-in pacing on every request, and every page was fetched at most twice and then cached locally.

TREE: taken from two independent sources that agree exactly. (1) https://www.roomandboard.com/catalog/sitemap - R&B's own full department -> section -> node listing; its Bath block reads Bath / Furniture (Vanities, Mirrors & Medicine Cabinets, Storage, Benches & Stools) / Lighting (Wall Sconces, Ceiling Lights, Pendant Lights) / Hardware & Organization (Bath Hardware, Organization, Hooks Shelves & Ledges, Cabinet Hardware) / Accessories (Bath Linens, Laundry, Self Care & Wellness, Rugs). (2) The schema.org SiteNavigationElement graph embedded in every page as script.schema-top-menu-data (255 nodes), which lists the same Bath URLs plus the cross-department bath nodes /catalog/storage-and-entryway/bath-storage-and-organization, /catalog/lighting/bath-lighting, /catalog/rugs/bath-rugs, /catalog/made-for-you/custom-bathroom-mirrors and /clearance/bath. I opened every one of those nodes and read its __NEXT_DATA__.

LEVEL DETECTION: R&B's page model self-identifies the level in props.pageProps.documentType. /catalog/bath is CATEGORY (department, no productGroups). /catalog/bath/bath-furniture, /catalog/bath/lighting, /catalog/bath/hardware-and-organization and /catalog/bath/bath-accessories are all INTERMEDIATE_CATEGORY - pure grouping pages carrying NO productGroups array at all - so each is emitted as a grouping row with blank qty and blank link and none of their URLs was recorded (rule 24). Only documentType=STANDARD nodes carry a listing and became leaves. /catalog/storage-and-entryway/bath-storage-and-organization is documentType=EDITORIAL with no productGroups - a curated landing page - and was excluded (rules 25, 27). /catalog/made-for-you/all-custom-mirrors is INTERMEDIATE_CATEGORY with 0 productGroups, so its child /catalog/made-for-you/custom-bathroom-mirrors (STANDARD, 7) is the leaf recorded.

QTY METHOD: Room & Board publishes NO 'N items' header anywhere on a PLP and exposes no count API - the document object's only integer fields are version, id and columnLayout, and there is no total, resultCount, numFound or nbHits anywhere in the payload. Each PLP also server-renders its ENTIRE listing with no pagination: grepping every recorded page for "pagination", 'load more' and nextPage returns 0 hits. So every qty is a full enumeration of props.pageProps.document.productGroups. VERIFICATION - two independent measures on every recorded leaf: I counted the productGroups array AND separately counted the distinct rendered anchor hrefs of the form <node-path>/<product-slug> in the HTML. They agreed exactly on all of them: Vanities 14=14, Mirrors & Medicine Cabinets 35=35, Bath Storage 8=8, Bath Hardware 19=19, Bath Organization 42=42, Hooks Shelves & Ledges 36=36, Laundry 7=7, Custom Bathroom Mirrors 7=7. Counts discriminate properly (7 to 42), none is a round display cap, every page's H1 matched the node requested, and no parent number was ever reused for a child - all four intermediate pages carry no number at all, so aggregation was impossible by construction.

CLASSIFICATION LINE USED. I kept a Bath node in rows only when BOTH (a) its __NEXT_DATA__ canonicalUrl points at itself, i.e. R&B genuinely owns it as a Bath node rather than aliasing a node from another department, AND (b) its primary product type appears in the Bathroom rules' own include lists. That produced: Vanities (rule 9 vanity units - all 14 groups are literally named '<name> Bathroom Vanities'); Mirrors & Medicine Cabinets (rule 10, which forbids skipping bathroom/vanity mirrors, and explicitly covers mirrored/medicine cabinets - 14 of the 35 groups are named Bath mirrors, e.g. Industry Bath Wall Mirrors, Infinity Arched Bath Floor Mirrors, Soho Bath Wall Mirrors, plus Bridger/Harlan Medicine Cabinets and Bridger Medicine Cabinet Sets); Bath Storage (rule 12 - Berkeley/Linear Linen Cabinets, Bridger Floating Linen Cabinet, medicine cabinets); Bath Hardware (rule 17 - Bend/Filmore/Hoff/Slim Towel Bars and Toilet Paper Holders, Sawyer Shower Caddies and Shower Shelves, Slim Freestanding Towel Rack); Bath Organization (rules 12/13 - Artemis Soap Dish, Artemis Bathtub Tray, Saco Toothbrush Holder, Saco Tumbler, Saco Soap Trays, Bend Toilet Paper Storage, Paros Tissue Box Covers, Mackey Waste Basket, Sawyer Shower Caddies); Hooks, Shelves & Ledges (rule 17 - Bathroom Hooks and Bathroom Shelves; self-canonical Bath node containing Sawyer Shower Caddies/Shelves and Stowe Wall Shelves with Towel Bar); Laundry (rules 12/13 bathroom baskets and storage - Kori Hampers plus Fletcher/Twain/Zelig/Surjo/Wolof baskets); and Made for You > Bathroom Mirrors (rule 10 - all 7 groups are Custom Bath Wall/Floor Mirrors).

CROSS-LISTING DISCLOSED HONESTLY: R&B merchandises one accessory assortment across several departments, so some products in the kept nodes also appear elsewhere - Hooks, Shelves & Ledges (36) overlaps /catalog/home-decor/shelves-and-ledges (27) and /catalog/storage-and-entryway/coat-racks (16), and Laundry (7) shares 6 of its 7 groups with /catalog/dining-and-kitchen/baskets-and-bins (16). I kept both because each is self-canonical under /catalog/bath/, sits inside R&B's own Bath hierarchy, and its product type is named in rules 12/13/17, which is exactly the case rule 30-33 resolves in favour of Bathroom ('Storage > Storage Baskets = Storage. Bathroom > Bathroom Baskets = Bathroom'). The Bath nodes that FAILED the canonical test or the product-type test were routed out instead and are all in review with their counts and URLs, so nothing is silently skipped. Confidence on Hooks/Shelves & Ledges and Laundry is the lowest of the kept set - flagging that here rather than in review because both are genuine, self-canonical Bath nodes.

DUPLICATES: no URL appears twice. /catalog/rugs/bath-rugs is reached from both Bath > Accessories > Rugs and the Rugs department but is one node, one review record (rule 28). /catalog/bath/cabinet-hardware and /catalog/home-decor/cabinet-hardware are the same 8-product node; only the Bath path is recorded, in review.

ALSO EXCLUDED: /clearance/bath (clearance listing, rule 25); /catalog/storage-and-entryway/bath-storage-and-organization (EDITORIAL, no listing); /catalog/made-for-you/custom-mirrors (7 groups - Industry/Infinity/Soho Custom Wall and Floor Mirrors, i.e. the NON-bath variants of the same programmes, a Decor node) and /catalog/made-for-you/all-custom-mirrors (intermediate); /catalog/home-decor/mirrors and /catalog/storage-and-entryway/mirrors (general decorative wall mirrors with no bathroom framing - rule 29 disambiguation, the word 'mirror' alone does not make them Bathroom, and the bath-specific mirrors are already captured by the two nodes above). FIXTURES: Room & Board sells no sanitaryware, baths, bathtubs, showers, enclosures, screens, toilets, bidets, basins or taps - regexing the full 235-link /catalog/sitemap for shower, toilet, sink, basin, faucet, tap, bathtub returns nothing beyond the Sawyer shower caddy/shelf products inside Bath Hardware. || CROSS-FILE DEDUP: 2 leaf record(s) removed as already extracted in a prior category workbook. See Review sheet.
